name: fcntl
synopsis: int fcntl(int fd, int op, ... /* arg*/);
description: The fcntl() system call performs various operations on an open file descriptor, such as duplicating it, setting flags, or managing locks. The operation is determined by the op argument, which may require an optional third argument.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: The file descriptor to operate on

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: The operation to perform, such as F_DUPFD or F_SETFD

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: Optional third argument, type and requirement depend on the operation (e.g., int for F_DUPFD, struct flock * for F_SETLK)

return_value.success: Varies by operation, such as the new file descriptor for F_DUPFD or zero for most other operations
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Operation is prohibited by locks held by other processes
fd is not an open file descriptor
op is F_SETPIPE_SZ and the new pipe capacity is smaller than the current buffer, or op is F_ADD_SEALS with conflicting conditions
lock structure is outside accessible address space
Invalid operation or argument, such as unrecognized op value
Per-process limit on open file descriptors reached for F_DUPFD
Too many segment locks or locking protocol failed
Operation not permitted, such as attempting to add seals without write access

bugs: The Linux implementation of mandatory locking is unreliable and has been deprecated in newer kernels; race conditions may occur in multithreaded programs when setting close-on-exec flags.
versions: Various operations since Linux 2.4 and later, with specific features like F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC since Linux 2.6.24
